transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, hi Doctor. I guess, um, well, it's a bit of a long story. I haven't been working for a while, just spending my time at home, and I think my daily routines have just gotten completely out of whack. My husband has been pointing out little things here and there, but what finally pushed me to actually pick up the phone and come in today is that my eating has just been completely all over the place lately. 

I mean, it's completely unpredictable and it's really starting to bother me. Some weeks, I'll cook a nice meal and I just barely touch my dinner. I'll just sit there pushing the food around my plate, not hungry in the slightest, even if it's something I usually love. I just have absolutely no taste for it. But then... then there are these other nights where it's the exact opposite. I'll wait until the house is completely quiet and everyone has gone to bed, and I'll just find myself standing there in the middle of the kitchen. Just standing right at the counter in the dark, eating crackers and sweets and whatever else I can find in the pantry. Just mindlessly eating sleeve after sleeve of crackers. And it's so frustrating because I used to be very regular about my meals back when I was taking classes, you know, breakfast, lunch, and dinner, but now it's like I have absolutely no rhythm or control over it whatsoever, and I just don't understand why my body is acting this way.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities that you once found pleasurable?

Well, yes, actually. That’s... that’s exactly how it feels, and it’s been weighing on me quite a bit. I used to be a very active person, you know? I mean, not running marathons or anything, but my weeks were always full of things I genuinely loved doing. But lately, it's like someone just turned the dial down on everything. 

Things I used to really look forward to just feel incredibly heavy now. Like my book club, for instance. We’ve been meeting for years, usually every second Tuesday, and I used to be the one who would read the book weeks in advance and bake something nice to bring over. Or going to the art galleries downtown on the weekends, or even just cooking a nice meal from scratch. I also have these rose beds in the backyard—beautiful heirloom roses that took me seasons to get right—and I used to spend hours out there pruning and weeding and just enjoying the sunshine. 

But now? Now it all just feels like... well, like chores that I keep putting off. I look out the kitchen window at the roses and all I can think about is how much effort it takes to go find my gardening gloves, so I just don't go out there. And the book club emails just pile up in my inbox because the thought of reading even a single chapter feels like climbing a mountain. It’s all just another task on a to-do list that I can’t bring myself to look at. I just keep procrastinating on my own life, I guess, and I don't understand where all my passion for these things went.
Have you been having any trouble with your sleep lately—like difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up earlier than planned?

Well, sleep is... it's a whole other story right now, honestly. You asked about trouble sleeping, but it doesn't really feel like trouble to me, if that makes sense? I mean, my husband certainly thinks it's a problem because I'm up and about making noise, but I actually feel fantastic when it happens. It’s just that my schedule is completely, totally upside down lately. 

I’ll go to bed, maybe around midnight or one in the morning, thinking I'll get a normal, full night's rest, but then—boom—my eyes just snap open. It's usually only after, I don't know, maybe three or four hours of sleep at the absolute most. But the strange part, the part I really don't understand, is that I don't feel tired at all. Not even a little bit groggy like you normally would if you woke up at three or four in the morning. I wake up feeling completely charged. Like there's actual electricity buzzing in my veins and I just have to get moving. 

And I just can't stay in bed when I feel like that, tossing and turning is just agonizing. So I get up, I tip-toe out to the kitchen to make a cup of tea, and I just start doing things. I've been writing all these blog posts—I used to have this little lifestyle and gardening blog years ago when I was taking classes, and suddenly I just have all these ideas for it again, pouring out of me. So I'm sitting there at the computer in the dark just typing away, or I'm planning out all these massive projects, like sketching out new organizational systems for the entire house or mapping out a whole new layout for the patio, all before the sun is even up. 

And it's so quiet then, you know? Just me and the glowing computer screen and the hum of the refrigerator. I actually get so much done in those early hours. It's just... well, three or four hours is really all my body seems to need right now. My brain is just firing on all cylinders, ready to go, and I don't even need an alarm clock anymore. My body just decides it's time to conquer the world in the pitch black. So, I guess I am waking up earlier than planned, but it feels incredibly productive, even if it is completely out of nowhere.
Have you ever experienced a period of time where you felt unusually high, excited, or irritable—like your energy or mood was significantly elevated for several days or more?

Well, yes, actually. Now that you mention it, that's exactly what happens. There are these stretches of time—like I was saying with the blog posts and the patio layout—where I just feel so... bright. Like everything is illuminated and I am just completely unstoppable. I'll have all these projects going at once, and I feel on top of the world, just absolutely glowing with energy and purpose. 

I'll pull out all my old watercolor paints from when I took that community college class years ago, and I'll spread them all over the dining room table, totally convinced I'm going to create a whole series of landscapes. And the ideas are just flowing! But the thing is, it doesn't always stay that pleasant. Or rather, the energy stays, but the mood just flips. Like a switch. I can go from feeling like I'm conquering the universe to being just absolutely furious. 

And I mean furious over the tiniest, most insignificant things. Like, my husband, bless his heart, he'll just be trying to set the table for dinner, and he'll move my paints just a few inches to the left to make room for a placemat, and I will just explode. I'll feel this blinding rage that he's disrupting my creative process, even though I had just left them there. Or he'll see a receipt from the craft store sitting on the counter and just casually ask, "Oh, did you buy more brushes?" and I will completely lose my temper. I'll yell at him for interrogating me and questioning my choices, and I'll feel so incredibly insulted that he would even ask about a piece of paper on the counter. 

It's like, one minute I'm flying high, completely untouchable, and the next minute I'm screaming about a receipt for a five-dollar brush and feeling like he's trying to ruin my life. It's so intense, that feeling of being unstoppable, but the irritability that comes with it the second someone gets in my way or questions me... it's really something else. I just feel so much all at once, and it can last for days where I'm just bouncing between feeling like a genius and feeling ready to bite someone's head off over a misplaced tube of paint.
Have you had episodes of depression like this before, or is this the first time you've felt this way?

Oh, no, it's definitely not the first time. I really wish it were, but... no, this has happened before. It’s something that just seems to creep up on me every so often, these long stretches I go through. And it’s so strange, you know, because you’d think there would be a reason for it, like a trigger or some awful news on the television, but there usually isn't. 

I'll just wake up one morning and the whole house... it just feels completely different. It feels so gray, like all the color has been completely washed out of the walls and the furniture, and the air itself just feels incredibly heavy. I'll find myself just sitting there at the kitchen table—it's this big oak table we've had forever, right by the window where I usually like to look out at the yard—and I'll just sit there feeling completely, utterly empty. Just hollowed out. 

And I'll sit there for what feels like hours, just staring at the grain of the wood or the sugar bowl, trying to figure out why I feel so awful, but the truth is, nothing terrible has happened that day! Absolutely nothing. The mail came, the weather was fine, just a perfectly normal Tuesday, but inside I just have this crushing emptiness. It’s so frustrating because my husband will come in and ask what’s wrong, or if something happened, and I can't even give him a good answer because I don't know myself. I just know that the house feels thick and gray, and that emptiness at the kitchen table is just... it's just there, taking up all the space where my normal feelings should be. So, yes, I've definitely had these periods before. They just kind of roll in like a fog and sit there, making everything heavy, even when my life is otherwise perfectly fine.
